sum.24: David asks God to guide him, to teach him his ways, and not to let him be put to shame, because he trusts in Him. He acknowledges that God is good, forgives sins, and teaches the humble and those who revere Him. In his loneliness and distress, he cries out for forgiveness and deliverance, and he also prays for Israel.
sum.60: David asks God to hear his cry and lead him to a rock higher than himself when his heart grows faint, because God has been his refuge and strong tower. He longs to live safely under the shelter of God's wings, prays for the long life of the king, and promises to praise God and fulfill his vows every day.
sum.68: David cries out to God from a suffering so deep that he feels like he is sinking into floodwaters and mud. He is rejected and mistreated for no reason, yet he trusts in God's mercy and asks to be rescued. In the end he promises to praise God, and he affirms that God listens to the needy and will keep his people safe.
sum.148: The psalmist invites God's people to sing a new song to him, with dancing, tambourine, and harp, because God takes delight in his people and gives victory to the humble. The faithful rejoice with praise, and with swords in their hands they carry out judgment on the nations. How to understand this image of judgment is interpreted in several ways.
sum.118: This psalm celebrates God's law as a path to life, a light for one's steps, and a treasure sweeter than honey. The psalmist asks for help to obey, for teaching, and for comfort, while suffering mockery and persecution from the arrogant. Even so, he trusts in God's eternal word. The text breaks off at verse 123.
sum.84: The sons of Korah remember that God was good to his land, for he forgave the sins of his people and restored them. Now they ask him to bring them back to life and to show them his mercy. They wait with confidence for his word of peace, for where mercy, truth, justice, and peace meet, the land yields its fruit.
sum.23: Psalm 24 says that the earth and everything in it belong to God, because he founded it. It asks who may come up to his holy mountain, and answers that it is the one with clean hands and a pure heart, who seeks God. It ends by calling on the ancient gates to open so that the King of glory, the mighty Lord, may come in.
sum.22: David says that Jehovah is his shepherd, so he will lack nothing. God takes care of him, gives him rest, restores him, and guides him along good paths. Even in the darkest valley he is not afraid, because God is with him and protects him. In the end he trusts that God's goodness and faithful love will follow him always, and that he will dwell in God's house.
sum.145: The psalmist resolves to praise God for as long as he lives and warns that we should not put our trust in rulers or in any human being, because all people die and their plans come to an end. Instead, the one who is happy is the one who puts their hope in God, the faithful Creator who brings about justice, gives bread to the hungry, sets prisoners free, sustains the orphan and the widow, and reigns forever.
sum.128: In this psalm, Israel remembers that from its youth it has suffered greatly, as if its back had been plowed with long furrows, but its enemies never managed to defeat it. God is righteous, and He broke the ropes of the wicked. Those who hate Zion will be put to shame and will wither like the grass on the rooftops, producing no fruit and receiving no blessing.
sum.56: David, fleeing from Saul and hiding in a cave, cries out to God for mercy and takes refuge in the shadow of His wings. Although he feels surrounded by enemies like lions, and they have set traps for him, he trusts that God will save him. He ends by singing praises, because God's mercy and truth are as great as the heavens.
sum.57: David rebukes corrupt judges who claim to act justly but practice wickedness and violence, and he compares them to poisonous snakes that refuse to listen. He asks God to break their power and remove them from the way. In the end, the righteous rejoice when they see that God judges on the earth and that there is a reward for those who remain faithful to him.
sum.8: David praised God with his whole heart because He had defended him and judged with justice, defeating his enemies. God reigns forever, is a refuge for the poor, and does not forget those who seek Him. David asks for mercy and for God to rise up, so that the nations will recognize that they are only human.
sum.105: The psalmist praises God for his goodness and confesses that Israel, just like their ancestors, rebelled again and again: at the Red Sea, with the golden calf, in the wilderness, and with the idols of Canaan. Even so, God saved them, heard their cry, and remembered his covenant. The psalm ends by asking God to gather his people together and by blessing him.
sum.112: Psalm 113 calls God's servants to praise his name at all times and in every place, from where the sun rises to where it sets. God is exalted above all nations and above the heavens, yet he still stoops down to look at the earth. He lifts up the poor and the needy, and gives the childless woman a home filled with joy.
sum.135: The psalm calls on us to give thanks to God because he is good, and his steadfast love endures forever, a phrase repeated in every verse. It recalls what God did in creating the heavens and the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars, and in freeing Israel from Egypt, guiding them through the wilderness, and giving them a land. It also emphasizes that God remembers his people in their humiliation and provides food for all.
sum.55: David, pursued by his enemies when the Philistines seized him in Gath, pleads with God for mercy. He admits that he feels afraid, but he chooses to trust God and His word. He believes God sees his tears and will deliver him, so he vows to give Him praise and to walk before Him in the light.
sum.100: David sings to God about his commitment to live with integrity, beginning in his own household. He promises to reject wickedness, slander, arrogance, deceit, and lies, and to seek out faithful people so they can be with him. He also intends to remove the wicked from the city of the LORD, so that justice may reign there.
sum.58: David prays to God when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him. He asks God to rescue him from violent enemies who lie, and he says they attack him even though he has done nothing wrong. Although he asks for justice against them, he ends with confidence, singing that God is his stronghold, his refuge, and his protection in times of distress.
sum.103: The psalmist praises God as Creator. He is shown clothed in light, establishing the earth, setting limits for the waters, and providing water, food, and shelter for all his creatures. Every living thing depends on his hand and on his Spirit. For this reason the psalmist vows to sing to him all his life, and expresses the wish that the wicked would disappear.
sum.130: In this psalm, David tells the LORD that his heart is not proud and that he does not pursue great things that are beyond his reach. He has calmed and quieted his soul, which rests in peace like a weaned child beside its mother. Then he invites Israel to put its hope in the LORD, now and forever.
sum.106: Psalm 107 calls people to give thanks to God because his mercy endures forever. It describes four groups in trouble: those lost in the desert, those imprisoned for their rebellion, those made sick by their foolishness, and sailors caught in a storm. In each case, they cry out to God, and he rescues them. The psalm ends by inviting the wise to reflect on his mercy.
sum.138: David praises God because He knows him completely: his thoughts, his ways, and even his words before he speaks them. There is nowhere to run from God's presence, whether in light or in darkness, and God carefully formed him in the womb. At the end, he rejects evil and asks God to examine his heart and lead him.
sum.48: The psalmist calls everyone, rich and poor alike, to listen to his wisdom: no one can buy back their life or escape death, and riches stay behind here on earth. Whoever trusts in their money and does not understand ends up like the animals that perish. But he trusts that God will redeem his life from the power of the grave, so there is no need to fear the rich.
sum.53: David prays to God for help when the Ziphites betray him to Saul. Violent men who have no regard for God are seeking his life. He trusts that God is his helper and his support, and he asks that his enemies receive what they deserve. David promises to offer sacrifices and to praise God's name, because God is good and has rescued him from distress.
sum.90: This psalm teaches that whoever lives trusting in God finds in him refuge and protection against dangers, plagues, and fears. God promises to watch over that person with his angels, to be with him in distress, to rescue him, and to honor him. In the end, he gives him a long life and shows him his salvation.
sum.1: The kings and nations rebel against God and his anointed one, and they want to free themselves from his authority. God laughs at them and declares that he has set his King on Zion, whom he calls his Son and to whom he promises the nations. The psalm ends by inviting rulers to serve the Lord with reverence and to put their trust in him.
sum.50: David prays to God after his sin with Bathsheba and asks for forgiveness, cleansing, and a new heart. He admits his guilt, pleads that God will not take his Spirit away from him, and asks to have his joy restored. He learns that God does not want sacrifices alone, but a humble and broken heart.
sum.39: David tells how he waited patiently for God, and God lifted him out of the mud and set him on a rock and put a new song in his mouth. He says that obeying God pleases him more than sacrifices, and that he has proclaimed God's righteousness to everyone. Even surrounded by troubles and sins, he asks for help and trusts that God will not delay.
sum.27: David cries out to God, asking him to hear him and not to leave him like those who go down to the grave. He pleads that he not be lumped together with the wicked, who speak peace to their neighbors while carrying evil in their hearts. He asks that God repay them according to their deeds. Then David praises God because he has heard his voice, come to his aid, and is his strength and shield. He prays that God would care for his people like a shepherd.
sum.62: David, in the desert of Judah, says he thirsts for God the way someone in a dry land thirsts for water, and that God's love is worth more than life itself. So he praises him, remembers him at night, and feels upheld in the shadow of his wings. He trusts that those who seek to destroy him will fall, while the king will rejoice in God.
sum.127: This psalm teaches that whoever fears the LORD and walks in his ways is happy and receives blessing. They will enjoy the fruit of their labor, and their family will be like a fruitful vine and like olive shoots around their table. It ends by asking that God bless them from Zion, that they see their grandchildren, and that there be peace over Israel.
sum.81: In this psalm by Asaph, God appears in judgment within the assembly of the "gods," who are rulers or judges acting unjustly and favoring the wicked. He orders them to defend the poor, the fatherless, and the needy, and warns them that, although they are called gods, they will die like any other human being. The psalmist ends by asking God to judge the earth.
sum.114: The psalmist asks that all the glory go to God, not to his people, and says that our God is in heaven and does whatever he pleases. The idols of silver and gold cannot speak, see, or walk, and those who trust in them become like them. For this reason Israel should trust in the LORD, who helps, protects, and blesses, and his people will praise him forever.
sum.19: This psalm is a prayer of the people for their king before a day of conflict, asking that God hear him, help him from Zion, and grant his desires. Then they declare with confidence that God saves his anointed. It teaches that, although others trust in chariots and horses, they will trust in the name of the LORD and remain steadfast.
sum.80: The psalmist calls the people to sing joyfully to God and to celebrate their festivals with music. God reminds them that he brought them out of Egypt and asks that they worship him alone. He laments that Israel did not listen to him, and says that if they had obeyed him, he would have protected them and fed them abundantly.
sum.15: David asks God to keep him safe because he trusts in him, and he declares that the LORD is his greatest treasure and his beautiful inheritance. He rejects those who chase after other gods, rejoices in God's counsel, and feels secure with God at his side. He ends by trusting that God will not leave him in the grave, and that God will show him the path of life, with fullness of joy.
sum.41: The psalmist, far from the temple and harassed by those who mock his faith, feels a deep thirst for God, like a deer that longs for water. He weeps, sadly remembers the festivals of praise, and feels overwhelmed, but he speaks to himself: he must wait for God, whom he will still praise.
sum.16: David prays to God in sincerity and asks for justice, protection, and for God to keep him safe as the apple of His eye. He describes his enemies as proud, greedy, and dangerous as lions, people who live only for this life. He, on the other hand, hopes to see God's face and to be satisfied.
sum.115: The psalmist loves God because God listened to him when he was close to death, distressed, and rescued him. Overflowing with gratitude, he asks what he can give back to the Lord, and he resolves to call on God, keep his vows, and offer praise before all his people in Jerusalem.
sum.96: Psalm 97 proclaims that the LORD reigns with justice and power, and that the whole earth trembles before his glory. The idols are put to shame, because he is far greater than all the gods. To those who love him, God keeps them safe from evil and gives them light and joy, and he invites the righteous to praise him.
sum.17: David sings of his love for and trust in the LORD, his rock and his deliverer, who rescued him from death, from his enemies, and from Saul. He describes in powerful images how God rose up with earthquake, fire, and storm to save him, and how He gave him strength and victory. He ends by praising God among the nations for His faithfulness to the king He anointed.
sum.35: David describes how the wicked person lives deceived, with no fear of God, and plans and speaks evil even while lying in bed. Then he praises God's love, faithfulness, and justice, which are as vast as the heavens and as high as the mountains. God is the source of life and a refuge, and David asks for protection against the proud, who in the end will fall.
sum.97: The psalmist calls everyone to sing a new song to God, because He has done wonderful things, has saved His people, and has shown His righteousness to the nations. Faithful to His mercy toward Israel, He receives praise with harps, trumpets, and voices. Even the sea, the rivers, and the mountains rejoice, because He is coming to judge the world with righteousness and fairness.
sum.64: David praises God in Zion because He hears prayer, forgives rebellions, and draws His people close to His house. He also exalts Him as the one who sets the mountains in place and calms the seas. In addition, he celebrates Him because He cares for the land with rain and crowns it with harvests, and all creation sings for joy.
sum.4: David prays to God in the morning and asks him to listen, because God rejects wickedness, lies, and deceit. He begs God to guide him in the face of his enemies, who speak falsely, and to stop them. He concludes by saying that those who trust in God will rejoice, since God blesses and protects the righteous like a shield.
sum.26: David trusts that Jehovah is his light and his strength, so he is not afraid of his enemies, even when they surround him and make war on him. His greatest desire is to live close to God, and he asks for guidance, help, and protection, even if his own family were to abandon him. He ends by encouraging readers to wait for Jehovah with courage and strength.
sum.116: This psalm, the shortest in the Bible, invites all nations and peoples to praise Jehovah. The reason is that his mercy toward us has been great, and his faithfulness endures forever. It ends with "Hallelujah," which means "praise Jehovah."
sum.10: David says that he trusts in Jehovah and rejects the advice to flee like a bird to the mountains, even though the wicked lie in wait in secret for the upright and seem to shake the foundations. But Jehovah rules from heaven, sees everything, tests the righteous, and will judge the wicked. The righteous, on the other hand, will see his face.
sum.126: This psalm, attributed to Solomon, teaches that without God's blessing, work and guarding the city are pointless, and that toiling without rest is in vain, because God gives sleep to those he loves. It also presents children as a gift and inheritance from the Lord, likened to arrows in the hand of a warrior, and the man who has many of them is blessed.
sum.54: David cried out to God with a heart full of fear because of the violence in the city and the betrayal of a close friend, and he longed to fly far away like a dove. He asked God to bring justice, yet he resolved to pray at all hours and to trust in Him. It teaches us to cast our burden on the Lord, who sustains the righteous.
sum.31: David tells how, while he kept his sin to himself, he wasted away and was in anguish, but when he confessed it to God, he received forgiveness. For this reason he encourages everyone to pray to God and to trust in Him as a refuge, without being stubborn like a horse or a mule. At the end he invites the righteous to rejoice and sing.
sum.42: The psalmist asks God to defend him against wicked and deceitful people, and he wonders why he feels rejected and sad because of the enemy's oppression. He begs that God's light and truth will guide him to God's holy mountain and altar, where he will praise God with joy. In the end, he encourages himself to keep hoping in God.
sum.125: This psalm speaks of the joy that will come when God brings his people back from captivity. It will be so great that it will seem like a dream, and even the other nations will take notice of what God has done. The psalmist asks that God restore his people, and teaches that those who sow in tears will reap with joy.
sum.132: The psalm celebrates how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity. It compares that unity to precious oil that runs down from the head of Aaron to the collar of his robe, and to the dew of Mount Hermon that falls on Zion. There, it says, the LORD commands blessing and eternal life.
sum.91: This psalm is a song for the Sabbath that invites people to praise God with music for his goodness and his great works. The wicked seem to flourish like grass, but they will be destroyed, while God remains forever on high. The righteous, by contrast, will flourish like the palm tree, bear fruit even in old age, and proclaim that God is upright.
sum.47: The psalm praises God as the great King who protects Zion, his city. Enemy kings gathered together, but when they saw it they were terrified and fled. So the people trust in God's steadfast love, walk around the city and count its towers, and they pass this on to the next generation: this God will guide us forever.
sum.43: The sons of Korah remember how God gave victory to their ancestors and declare that they trust in Him alone. But now they suffer defeat and mockery, although they say they have not abandoned His covenant. With sincerity they ask God to awake, to help them, and to redeem them according to His mercy.
sum.28: David invites everyone to give God the glory and worship He deserves. He describes the voice of the LORD as a powerful force that thunders over the waters, breaks the cedars, makes the wilderness tremble, and fills His temple with praise. God reigns forever, and He gives strength and peace to His people.
sum.117: The psalmist calls everyone to praise God because his faithful love lasts forever. He tells how, surrounded by enemies, he cried out to God and was rescued, and so trusting in God is better than trusting in people. He then enters the temple with joy, grateful for the salvation he has received, and lifts up God in praise.
sum.9: In this psalm, the psalmist asks God why He seems to be far away while the wicked, proud and deceitful person hunts down the poor and thinks God does not see. But he trusts that God does see the suffering, and he asks Him to rise up. God is the eternal King, He hears the humble, and He defends the orphan and the poor.
sum.34: David cried out to God in the middle of unfair persecution. He asked God to defend him against enemies who had repaid his kindness with harm, even though he had prayed and fasted for them. He trusts that God has seen what happened and will rescue him. He promises to praise God publicly, because God cares for those who are suffering.
sum.122: In this psalm, the people lift their eyes to God, who reigns in the heavens, and they trust in Him the way servants watch the hand of their masters, waiting for their help. They ask for mercy because they are tired of the contempt and mockery of the proud and careless. It teaches us to wait on God with humility when we feel humiliated.
sum.21: David cries out to God from deep suffering: he feels abandoned, mocked, and surrounded by enemies who wound him and divide his clothes among themselves. Even so, he remembers that God delivered his ancestors and asks for help. In the end he promises to praise God, and he affirms that God hears the afflicted and that all the nations will worship him.
sum.99: The psalmist calls on all the people of the earth to sing to God and to serve him with joy. He reminds them that the LORD is God, that he made us, and that we are his people, like sheep in his pasture. For this reason we should come into his presence with thankfulness and praise, because he is good, and his mercy and his faithfulness last forever.
sum.133: This short song calls on the servants of God who serve through the night in his house to praise him and to lift their hands toward the sanctuary. At the end, someone answers with a blessing: may God, the maker of heaven and earth, bless them from Zion. It teaches that worshiping God and receiving his blessing go together.
sum.14: In Psalm 15, David asks who may live near God, in His tent and on His holy hill. The answer describes a person of integrity who does what is right, speaks the truth, does not slander or harm their neighbor, honors those who fear God, keeps their word even when it costs them, does not lend money at exorbitant interest, and does not accept bribes. Anyone who lives this way will remain secure.
sum.0: Psalm 1 presents two ways of life. Happy is the person who does not follow the advice of the wicked, but who loves the law of the LORD and meditates on it day and night. That person is like a tree planted by water, which bears fruit in its season. The wicked, by contrast, are like chaff that the wind blows away, because the LORD watches over the way of the righteous.
sum.136: The exiles in Babylon weep when they remember Zion. They hang up their harps and refuse to sing for those who oppress them. They vow never to forget Jerusalem. At the end, they cry out to God for justice against Edom and Babylon, using very harsh words that show their deep pain.
sum.33: David praises God at all times, because God heard him and rescued him from his fears and troubles. He invites everyone to taste for themselves that God is good, and he teaches people to fear God, watch their words, turn away from evil, and pursue peace. God is close to those whose hearts are broken, and he redeems those who put their trust in him.
sum.49: In this psalm by Asaph, God calls to the whole earth and presents himself as the judge of his people. He tells them he does not need their animals, because everything belongs to him; what he wants is sincere thanksgiving, promises kept, and prayer in times of distress. He also rebukes the wicked hypocrite and calls him to turn back and reconsider.
sum.86: This psalm celebrates Zion as the city of God, founded on holy mountains and loved by the LORD more than any other place in Jacob. God recognizes people from nations such as Rahab, Babylon, Tyre, and Ethiopia as having been born there, and the singers rejoice, saying that all their springs are in her. Scholars interpret in various ways what this "birth" in Zion means.
sum.74: In this psalm, Asaph thanks God because he is near and does wonderful deeds. God answers that he will judge with justice at the appointed time, and that he holds up the earth when everything is shaking. He warns the proud not to lift up their heads, because only God brings down and lifts up, and the wicked will drink his cup, while the righteous will be raised up.
sum.72: Asaph confesses that he nearly stumbled in his faith when he saw the wicked prospering, and he came to think that remaining faithful was pointless. Everything changed when he entered God's sanctuary and understood their end, and he recognized his own blindness. Then he affirms that God is his guide, his strength, and his greatest good.
sum.111: Psalm 112 describes the man who fears God and delights in His commandments. He is righteous, compassionate, and generous to the poor. God blesses him and his children, and his memory endures. He does not live in fear, because he trusts in Jehovah. The wicked, by contrast, become angry when they see him, and their desires come to nothing.
sum.12: David cries out to God in pain, asking how long he will feel forgotten. His heart is full of anxiety, and his enemy has the upper hand. He asks God to look at him and answer him, and to restore his strength so that he does not fall and give his enemies something to celebrate. Even so, he ends by trusting in God's mercy and promising to sing to him for his goodness.
sum.13: David says that the fool thinks there is no God, and that people have become corrupt and no one does good. God looks down from heaven for anyone who seeks Him, but all have turned aside. The wicked oppress God's people and are filled with dread, because God is with the righteous; the psalmist longs for Israel's salvation.
